newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf heat oil diffs up late day in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf heat oil diffs up late day in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. Gulf (USG) No. 2 oil prices jumped higher Monday as differentials there continued to rebound from the recent weakness.
But market players said activity remained very subdued with many participants out between last week's Christmas holiday and the coming New Year's Day holiday on Wednesday.
"It's sloppy out there, and there's not much getting done," one trader said.
NYMEX January heating oil ended Monday a touch higher, while gasoline price dipped slightly. NYMEX will close early Tuesday and reopen Thursday in observance of the holiday.
USG prompt No. 2 was offered at 5.00 cents under the NYMEX for delivery in the back 36th cycle on the Colonial Pipeline, an increase of about 0.75 cent on the day.
USG No. 2 oil had been under pressure during the past several days after the Colonial said it would continue pro-rationing through January because of heavy demand.
USG low sulphur diesel was talked between 3.50 and 3.25 cents under the screen for the front 1st cycle on the Colonial, up more than 1 cent in very choppy trade, according to market players.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk 1 212 859 1620
